title: A copy does not say which version it is showing
goal: When a component has more than one version, the two originals in the layers list each say which version they are. A copy placed on the canvas does not: its row shows the component name and the copy mark and nothing else, so a copy switched to Disabled looks exactly like one left on Default. The canvas label and the Component panel both say it; the list should too.
notes: Reproduced 2026-09-07 with Scripts/playtest/version-row-name-walk.json: step 34 runs showNextComponentVersion on a placed copy, and the row in version-row-copy-sc.png still reads "Save button" with the outline mark and no version. Cause is PhotonzDocument.versionName(of:counts:) in Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerPanelTree.swift, which returns layer.componentVersionName, itself group?.versionName, and that is set on a main only. An instance carries its choice elsewhere (Layer.instanceVersion). The row has room for it now that the version prints under the name (LayersPanel.swift nameBlock).
acceptance: A copy showing a non-default version says so in its layers row
Switching a copy to another version changes what its row says, with no reselecting
A copy of a component that has only one version says nothing extra, as it does today

log.note: A placed copy now prints the version it is showing under its name in the layers list, using the one rule the canvas label already used: originals always speak, a copy speaks only when it is not on the first version. canvasVersionNames() and layerRows() share a single multiVersionComponents() pass so the two cannot disagree (Sources/PhotonzCore/ComponentVersions.swift, LayerPanelTree.swift), and a row carries the version in its playtest detail (Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift). Verified: two new ComponentVersionTests that fail on the old code, Scripts/test.sh green at 4778 tests, and version-row-name-walk.json on the probe reading the copy as "layer, showing the Disabled version" with a real screen capture.
